sourceDocument: Energy Planning Week 2026 - Draft Programme (overview), 23 September 2026

itemTypes.meal: Lunch or dinner, including working sessions over food

items.title: Opening session
items.subtitle: From COP31 commitments to investment-ready planning
items.summary: Welcome remarks by IRENA, GET.transform and the co-lead countries, followed by two introductory presentations: an overview of the LTES Network's work and the role of scenario practice in connecting national planning to policy and investment decisions; and GET.transform's support to countries across the planning-to-implementation chain.

items.title: Electrification and the COP commitments – what scenarios must now capture
items.summary: This opening session examines what accelerated electrification commitments mean for national energy planning. Government planners and the institutions supporting them discuss how global electrification goals translate into national scenarios, policies and investment pipelines, and what practical support countries need to make that translation work.
items.note: Scene-setting: outcomes of COP31 and SB64 relevant to electrification and planning.

items.title: Building planning ecosystems that survive political cycles
items.summary: Durable scenario work depends on institutions. This session examines how countries build planning ecosystems that develop and retain capacity across ministries, universities and research institutions, moving from dependence on external support toward self-sustaining national planning functions. It covers institutional mandates and ownership, skills and retention, modelling-tool institutionalisation, and alignment with policy and budget cycles.

items.title: Lunch break and poster session
items.summary: An extended lunch with a poster session: participants present scenario tools, country cases and ongoing work for informal discussion over lunch.

items.title: Data governance, sharing and quality assurance for developing long-term scenarios
items.summary: Credible scenarios rest on credible data, yet many planning teams face fragmented access, persistent gaps and heavy reliance on proprietary datasets. This session examines how countries and regional institutions govern, share and quality-assure energy data – from national energy information systems to regional databases – and explores practical solutions for planning teams with limited resources.

days.label: Day 2
days.theme: Scenarios for Security, Flexibility and Implementation

items.title: LTES Network members and partners strategic meeting
items.access: Closed-door — LTES Network members and partners only

items.title: Impact session: Brazil's national energy plan and the LTES Network
items.summary: Brazil's Energy Research Office presents the country's national energy planning instruments — the long-term PNE 2055 and the ten-year expansion plan PDE 2035 — and reflects on how peer exchange through the LTES Network informed national planning practice. An impact spotlight on what Network collaboration looks like for national planning processes.

items.title: Planning under geopolitical uncertainty
items.summary: Geopolitical volatility, fuel-price shocks and supply disruptions have moved energy security back to the centre of national planning. This session examines how countries stress-test scenarios against these risks, how the fossil-fuel transition and stranded-asset exposure are treated in national frameworks, and how alternative plans are conceived to respond to supply disruptions.

items.title: Lunch session: machine learning and artificial intelligence in energy planning
items.summary: A working-lunch, state-of-the-art showcase of applied AI uses prioritised by the LTES Network – demand and load forecasting, scenario development and sensitivity analysis, and data processing and quality assurance.

items.title: Climate risks and adaptation in national energy scenarios
items.summary: Climate variability and physical risks – heatwaves, floods, droughts and shifting hydrology – are stress-testing national energy systems in real time. This session examines how planning teams incorporate climate risks and adaptation into long-term scenarios: from El Niño-driven droughts in hydropower-dependent systems to cooling demand and flood exposure, and the data and methods needed to make plans resilient.

items.title: Transformative scenarios in national planning practice
items.summary: Scenario practice is evolving: deep uncertainty and robust decision-making, agent-based and participatory modelling, and open-source tools are moving from research into government planning, bringing new actors and interdisciplinary insights into the scenario-building process itself. This session examines how these methods can be navigated within the realities government planners face: resource constraints, institutional mandates and political viability.

items.title: Day 2 wrap and bridge to Day 3
items.summary: Joint reflections by IRENA and GET.transform.

days.label: Day 3
days.theme: From Planning to Investment and Implementation

items.title: Opening: from the LTES Forum to investment-ready implementation
Findings from the GCEP regional planning-to-investment dialogues
items.subtitle: What countries are telling us about planning, investment and implementation
items.summary: Cross-regional findings from the GCEP regional dialogues and other relevant regional exchanges, focusing on recurring planning-to-investment messages: grids and flexibility, institutional coordination, project preparation, finance-facing planning signals, data and governance, and country requests for practical partner support.

items.title: Global perspectives on the planning-to-investment gap
items.summary: Financiers from across regions examine the planning-to-investment challenges emerging from the regional dialogues: what do development banks and markets need to see in a national plan before capital moves? Drawing on experience from Latin America, Africa, Asia and Europe, the session identifies common barriers and practical lessons for turning long-term energy plans into implementable investments.

items.title: Planning the transition away from fossil fuels (TAFF)
items.summary: The transition away from fossil fuels (TAFF) agenda through the lens of investment-ready energy planning: how national planning systems can translate transition-away commitments into credible implementation pathways, and what practical support GCEP can provide to facilitate dialogue between planners, policymakers and financiers on the conditions needed to move from political commitment to investable action. It also reflects on the development and climate nexus.

items.title: From plans to delivery – how can planning support enabling energy markets?
items.summary: What it takes to turn energy planning priorities into commercially viable projects, infrastructure and functioning markets. The session looks at what needs to happen from planning to action — from policy, regulation and procurement to market design and investment decisions — and where key barriers can emerge along the way, bringing together perspectives from different actors on how governments and planning institutions can create the conditions for investment and strengthen the link between long-term planning and delivery.

items.title: Country cases – when planning meets the market
items.summary: Country case presentations from three angles. Planning enables the market (large scale): how long-term planning can inform large-scale project procurement and create a pipeline investors can respond to. The market moves faster than planning (distributed generation): what happens when markets, prosumers or new technologies such as battery storage move ahead of the assumptions in the plan, and how market information, investor behaviour, technology costs and emerging business models should feed back into planning. Planning enables infrastructure investment: how grid infrastructure enables functioning energy markets and private investment, and how planning can provide the long-term visibility, coordination and investment framework needed to develop it.

items.title: Closing of Energy Planning Week 2026
items.summary: Joint closing remarks by IRENA and GET.transform: what the week established — from scenario practice to planning-to-investment — and what follows: the partnerships, country cases and commitments carried forward into the GCEP programme and the LTES Network calendar for 2027.

days.label: Day 4

items.title: Partner-hosted sessions
items.summary: A day of sessions hosted by partner institutions, giving partners space to convene discussions with country teams on planning and implementation cases. Open to members and partners of GCEP, the LTES Network and GET.transform.
